key_insight: A sex-aware Transformer (STAGE-AD) found sex-dimorphic Alzheimer’s disease risk loci and linked them to likely causal cell-type regulatory circuits.
clinical_relevance: The work suggests that sex-specific genetic regulation could improve Alzheimer’s risk mapping and help guide more tailored biomarker and therapeutic research.
method: Analyzed 449,335 European-ancestry participants with sex-stratified and genotype-by-sex models.
Built STAGE-AD, a Transformer combining molecular QTLs, epigenomic features, and single-cell annotations.
Validated candidate genes and variant-to-cell/pathology chains using independent cohorts and multi-omics brain donor data.
evidence_signal: The model achieved a primary test-set PR-AUC of 0.895, but performance dropped to 0.751 with locus hold-out and 0.681 with APOE-region hold-out.
watch_item: Reported signals were provisional and model performance weakened under stricter hold-outs, so independent replication is still needed before translation.
paper_title: Sex-aware Cross-tissue Regulatory Transformer Identified Sexually Dimorphic Alzheimer's Disease Risk Loci and Causal Cellular Circuit
